Hannah / Marissa — thanks for the ping and the doc. Quick read; below are pragmatic options that balance legal risk and commercial needs.

Primary risks: public disclosures that reference performance figures or benchmarking could be viewed as endorsement or misrepresentation. Logo use can create trademark exposure if not covered by brand guidelines.

Suggested language (short form):
1) Announcement / References:
  - "Each party may make press announcements concerning the existence of the business relationship provided that the disclosing party provides the other party with a copy of the proposed press release and any associated materials at least seven (7) business days prior to publication for review and comment. Such review shall be limited to technical accuracy and trademark usage and shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed."

  - If Lumenics insists on a longer window, we can offer 14 business days but require that refusal be accompanied by specific, reasonably detailed objections.

2) Logo & Trademark Use:
  - "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to use Customer's name and logo solely to identify Customer as a Redwood customer in Redwood's marketing materials, subject to Customer's brand guidelines and prior written approval of any materials featuring the Customer logo. Approval shall not be unreasonably withheld and shall be provided within five (5) business days of request."

3) Confidentiality carve-out for benchmark/performance:
  - Keep performance metrics as Confidential Information but permit de-identified, aggregated benchmark references or customer-approved metrics only after written consent.

Operational/contract placement: we can add the announcement clause in the MSA (Publicity) and put granular controls (brand guidelines, logo files, approvals) in an Order Form addendum or a short "Marketing Addendum".

I'll prepare a redline draft for the MSA and a short one-page marketing addendum. If they refuse both, we could agree to a mutual announcement only after the first paid invoice is processed to give them more comfort.

—Dev
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for sending the redlines. We reviewed internally and propose the compromise below, attached as redlines to the MSA and a short Marketing Addendum (see attachments). Summary of proposed changes: 

1) Announcement & References: 7 business day review period for press releases and customer-facing materials; review limited to trademark/technical accuracy and shall not be unreasonably withheld. We can extend to 14 days only if Lumenics provides specific objections.

2) Logo Use: Redwood requests a non-exclusive revocable license to use the Lumenics name and logo for customer identification and marketing materials, conditioned on adherence to Lumenics' brand guidelines and a 5-business-day approval target for any use of the logo.

3) Performance Metrics: Performance and benchmark data remain Confidential Information. We can reference de-identified or aggregated metrics only with explicit written consent.

Commercial trade: We are prepared to offer a one-page case study and a product quote on our website in exchange for the shorter approval timeline. We will not accept any exclusivity in geography or vertical.

Next steps: I attached redlines (redwood_msa_redline_v2.pdf) and a short Marketing Addendum that captures the logo/license language. Please review and let us know if you can accept these in principle or if you prefer a short call with Dev/Marissa to walk through them. If you agree, we can send a DocuSign-ready set and aim to have this wrapped by May 7 to keep the pilot timeline intact.
